_note: v2 hook overrides for la rivière (B28_riviere). Source hooks are kept wherever the painting shows them; these replace only hooks whose painted scene differs from the source text.

fr_flux_noun.hook: Like English 'flux', said FLEW: the FLOOD TIDE foams so strongly that a startled duck is swept along, flapping its wings, as if it FLEW backwards.
fr_flux_noun.why: A duck flying backwards up the river cannot be painted clearly; the painting shows a startled duck flapping in the foaming flood tide.

fr_lac_noun.hook: Like English 'lake', said LAHK: a fisherman sits all day by the LAKE and moans about his LACK of fish, while a heron behind him gulps one down.
fr_lac_noun.why: The painted heron holds a single fish, not six.

fr_fontaine_noun.hook: Like English 'fountain', said fohn-TEHN: a FOUNTAIN in the park sprays its jets of water, and a duck leaps up to catch one.
fr_fontaine_noun.why: The painted fountain has a few jets, not ten, and one duck catching a jet.

fr_truite_noun.hook: A TROUT leaps out of the river for a treat ("TRWEET") and flips back in with a splash.
fr_truite_noun.why: A fish tweeting like a bird cannot be shown; the painting shows the trout leaping for the treat.

fr_canal_noun.hook: Sounds like 'can-ALL', said kah-NAHL: one giant tin CAN floats down the long straight CANAL carrying ALL the ducklings, with a heron riding at the back.
fr_canal_noun.why: Owner review: 'Al' was a weak hook; the painting now shows a giant tin-can boat carrying all the ducklings.

fr_fleuve_noun.hook: A RIVER full of floating hearts, LOVE ("FLUHV"), flows down through the valley on its long way to the sea.
fr_fleuve_noun.why: In the one-scene valley the hearts float down the river from the far hills; there is no beach in the painting.

fr_marais_noun.hook: A bride and groom marry ("mah-REH") on a little round wooden raft among the reeds of the MARSH: the bride wears a veil and a crown of daisies, the groom a top hat.
fr_marais_noun.why: Round 6 Lesson 2: the frog couple acting human was repainted as a human bride and groom on a raft among the marsh reeds. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (ma-RAY -> mah-REH).

fr_grenouille_noun.hook: A FROG sits in a big green ("gruh") bowl of noodles ("NOOY"), slurping a noodle.
fr_grenouille_noun.why: Only one frog is painted with the noodle bowl, sitting in it rather than leaping out.

fr_tombee_noun.hook: NIGHTFALL: the sun drops into the far bay ("tohn-BAY") of the lake behind the hills, as a girl sitting on a fence post opens a tome to read.
fr_tombee_noun.why: The crues scene was repainted as one river valley; the sun sets into a lake among the hills. Round 6 Lesson 2: the reading owl was repainted as a girl. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (ton-BAY -> tohn-BAY).

fr_crapaud_noun.hook: A fat warty TOAD squats on a wooden crate ("krah-POH"), right beside a little black toy piano nobody is playing.
fr_crapaud_noun.why: The toad IS the word, so it stays, but it no longer plays the piano like a person (LESSONS 2); it just sits on the crate by the piano. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (kra-PO -> krah-POH).

fr_aquarium_noun.hook: Like English 'aquarium', said ah-kwah-RYOM: a goldfish in an AQUARIUM on a little table by the lake stares out at a wild fish swimming outside the glass.
fr_aquarium_noun.why: Round 6 Lesson 2: the painted goldfish just looks out (no waving), so the hook no longer has it wave like a person.

fr_eau_noun.hook: "Oh!" ("OH") gasps a surprised water jug in a cottage window as fresh WATER splashes out of it.
fr_eau_noun.why: The painting shows the jug itself gasping 'Oh!' as water splashes out; there is no goldfish or bowl.

fr_inondation_noun.hook: A FLOOD — an inundation ("ee-nohn-dah-SYOHN") — fills the village streets; ducks paddle past the shops.
fr_inondation_noun.why: Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (ee-non-da-SYON -> ee-nohn-dah-SYOHN).
